findings.title: Plaintext passwords are written to logs on signup
findings.explanation: The PR description says the logger already redacts sensitive fields, but that is not true. `REDACTED_KEYS` in `src/lib/logger.ts` contains only `authorization` and `token`. `password` is not redacted, so `logger.info('signup attempt', { body: req.body })` writes the user's plaintext password to stdout, and from there to log aggregation and retention. The email and organization name (PII) are also logged. This is a credential leak and a likely compliance problem (GDPR, SOC2). Remove the line. If you need to debug validation failures, log only non-sensitive metadata, such as the field names present and the zod issue paths and codes. Do this in a `safeParse` failure branch, not with the raw body. Example: `logger.warn('signup validation failed', { issues: result.error.issues.map(i => ({ path: i.path, code: i.code })) })`. Also consider logging the keys of `req.body` and the content-type.

findings.title: Redaction list is too narrow for a deny-list approach
findings.explanation: The redaction list lacks `password`, `passwd`, `secret`, `api_key`, `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `cookie`, `card` and similar keys. It also matches keys only by exact name. Any future code that logs request bodies will leak in the same way. Extend the list, and consider case-insensitive substring or pattern matching. Better still, log an explicit allow-list of fields rather than whole bodies. Add a unit test that confirms `password` is redacted.

findings.title: Validation failures are not handled or logged in a useful way
findings.explanation: The real problem is that `signupSchema.parse` throws on invalid input, and the error handler in `server.ts` logs only `err.message`. Handle ZodError explicitly: use `safeParse`, return a 400 with the issues, and log the sanitized issues (paths and codes only). That shows why signups fail without logging the payload. The same applies to `/login`.
